title: mcp: the worker CPU-budget case in mcp-file-tools.test.ts depends on runner load and fails on unrelated PRs
body:
repo:objectstack#2 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmQ2SN4K183oqAvUajA

Filing gate ①: a timing-dependent test that failed twice today on PRs that do not touch `packages/mcp`. Dedupe: `mcp-file-tools`; no open card.

Suggested-grade: p2 · domain:server (`packages/mcp`) · tooling

## What happened

`packages/mcp/src/mcp-file-tools.test.ts`, case "out of CPU budget on the worker: the pages read so far, truncated, with the budget note, as in-process" (around line 950), failed in Test Core shard 3/8 on PR #34545 (run https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/44001704215; green on re-run) and again on PR #34719 at head `2a25dade9` today. Neither PR touches `packages/mcp`.

The case sets `cpuBudgetMs: 30` on the extraction worker and asserts that the read stops partway with the budget note. A 30 ms CPU budget on a loaded CI runner makes the stop point, and whether the warm-up is charged, depend on runner load.

## What is wanted

Make the case deterministic at the root: drive the budget from a controllable clock or a budget the fixture is sure to cross (and not cross on the warm read), so the assertion does not depend on runner load. ⛔ Not a skip, a retry wrapper or a looser assertion that stops pinning the truncation.

## Re-check

`git grep -n "cpuBudgetMs: 30" -- packages/mcp/src/mcp-file-tools.test.ts`
